build: Birzzle Fever iOS 1.0.4 with exact lower-case API allowlist, hostname, request-ID and NSError hooks
operator_observation: After a few seconds of loading animation, the same dialog appeared: Failed to connect to network. Please check network status.

static_analysis_after_capture.startup_native_callsite: 0x180b4e calls 0x205d74 with API literal server.init.2 at 0x38c658
static_analysis_after_capture.first_request_api_inference: server.init.2 is a strong candidate for first startup request, but the device trace redacted it and did not prove request-ID-to-caller correspondence. The literal contains a digit, so the installed diagnostic's old uppercase-dotted filter and 29-name lowercase allowlist both reject it.
static_analysis_after_capture.cross_platform_contract: The original read-only Android game library also contains the exact server.init.2 literal; its compiled client version differs from the iOS client's version. Historical Android SERVER.INIT cache has a JSON envelope but its requestversion differs from the iOS compiled client version.
static_analysis_after_capture.ios_save_storage: The iOS native save writer invokes SFHFKeychainUtils storeUsername:andPassword:forServiceName:updateExisting:error: with fixed BirzzleFeverUser account and a dynamic service name; the native reader invokes getPasswordForUsername:andServiceName:error:. Thus an app-container archive is not a Keychain save export. Cross-platform encrypted-file key agreement alone does not establish an iOS restore path.

next_action: Map the iOS Keychain service-key derivation and native offline response dispatch. privacy: No token, member identifier, UDID, account values, full URL, request parameters, or crash filename appears in this finding. Raw logs stay ignored under ios/captures; Android was inspected read-only.
